text: Paul's letters never say "our Father in heaven." Just "Abba, Father." You're no longer far away.
explanation:
When Jesus taught His disciples to pray "Our Father in heaven," He hadn't yet died and risen; they were on earth, and the Father was far above. After the resurrection He said, "I am ascending to My Father and your Father, to My God and your God." Then "because you are sons, God sent forth the Spirit of His Son into your hearts, crying out, 'Abba, Father!'"

In the epistles it's simply "Father," "our God and Father," "Abba." At Lazarus' tomb, Jesus didn't look up and say "Father in heaven," but "Father, I thank You that You have heard Me." That's the nearness He has given you. Say "Father," and know you're close.

text: Praying "in Jesus' name" isn't a phrase at the end. It's praying as if Jesus Himself were asking.
explanation:
In the upper room, Jesus told His disciples, "Until now you have asked nothing in My name. Ask, and you will receive, that your joy may be full." Yet the prayers recorded in the epistles don't end with "in the name of Jesus." Saying it is fine. But something more is meant.

An ambassador sent in his nation's name doesn't go as himself; he goes as his country. To ask in Jesus' name is to come conscious that you're accepted in His acceptance and loved with the love the Father has for Him. Come with that nearness, and pray.

text: You don't have to make your prayers long. The Father isn't impressed by vocabulary; He's moved by His children.
explanation:
Jesus warned against praying like those who "think they will be heard for their many words." Some prayers are really aimed at the people listening. And some believers come to God so afraid that they rush through their requests and leave, yet they'll chat for hours with a friend over coffee.

"You did not receive the spirit of bondage again to fear, but the Spirit of adoption by whom we cry out, 'Abba, Father.'" Notice the word "cry": it's spontaneous, a child calling for a dad. Sometimes the best prayer is just to linger in His presence and let Him love you.

text: The Lord's Prayer starts with three things about God, His name, kingdom and will, before three things we need: bread, forgiveness and deliverance.
explanation:
As a model, the prayer Jesus taught His disciples is perfection. It begins, "Hallowed be Your name. Your kingdom come. Your will be done," giving God His place first. Only then does it turn to us: "Give us this day our daily bread. Forgive us. Deliver us from the evil one."

Our prayers often start with "me, my, mine." Start with Him. You can still pray, "Give us this day our daily bread" and "Lead us not into temptation" every morning. But remember you're praying after the cross, as a forgiven child, not one hoping to earn forgiveness by how well you forgive.

text: "Prayer and supplication" in Philippians 4:6 are the same words as Ephesians 6:18, which adds "in the Spirit."
explanation:
"In everything by prayer and supplication, with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God; and the peace of God… will guard your hearts and minds." Ephesians uses the same pair of Greek words: "praying always with all prayer and supplication in the Spirit." Paul explains elsewhere: "If I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays… I will pray with the spirit, and I will also pray with the understanding."

When you don't know how to pray, or there's a knot in your stomach over a child or a situation you can't see clearly, your spirit can pray beyond your understanding. Your requests are "made known" (it's passive), and peace stands guard over your heart.

text: God didn't create you to get a servant. He has angels for that. He made you to have someone to love.
explanation:
If God only wanted service and worship, angels already sing with perfect pitch, never tire and never fall asleep during sermons. He made you for a different reason. Love's nature is to give, and perfect love longs for someone to pour itself out on.

Think of a parent coming home from a long trip, aching to hold their children. If an imperfect parent feels that way, how much more your perfect Father? You weren't made to keep God busy. You were made to be loved by Him.
